title: Tighten logit softcap 15 -> 10
description: One line in GPT.forward: softcap = 15 -> 10; nothing else touched. val_bpb 0.986373 vs baseline 0.986277 (a tie, +0.0001, inside the ~0.0009 noise floor).
reflection: Softcap is now measured on BOTH sides of 15 and 15 is the optimum. Round 6: s=30 cost +0.0040 (5 runs, unanimous). This round: s=10 is a dead tie (+0.0001) with slightly LOWER final train loss (2.765 vs ~2.768) at 1% less compute (328.2M tokens, MFU 38.09% vs 331.5M / 38.48%), params 71.3M and peak VRAM 32.9GB identical. So the curve is strongly asymmetric: loosening the cap hurts a lot, tightening it does nothing. That kills the simple 'softcap is a confidence regularizer whose strength we can dial' story I argued from -- if it were a regularizer on a smooth curve, more of it would have moved val_bpb in one direction or the other. The better reading is that the cap's job is bounding the logit/gradient scale during the high-LR Muon phase, and anything at or below ~15 bounds it adequately while 30 does not. Practically: the output head is now a CLOSED axis, in both directions, and should not take another slot. With 1 run left for the cell, the honest state of play is that every axis we have probed -- batch size, head split, depth, width, embedding capacity, softcap -- is flat or negative except depth 8->12, which is already banked in the baseline. The only regions never touched are the LR schedule constants (WARMUP_RATIO=0.0, WARMDOWN_RATIO=0.5, FINAL_LR_FRAC=0.0) and WINDOW_PATTERN; if the last run is spent, it should be spent there, not on another capacity or head-shape variant.
